text:
All five scope items are done; three were worse than recorded.

1. Canonical printer: three copies, not two. CanonicalRequest in ManagedModel had a
   third. Now one definition in core/codec/CanonicalJson, with laws in
   CanonicalJsonLawSuite stating what the consumers rely on (order-independence at
   every depth, explicit null retained, no insignificant whitespace) and a test in
   JournalReplayLawSuite pinning CanonicalRequest to the shared rendering.

2. IdentifierRules: no longer a byte-identical duplicate. core's copy had already
   been reduced to a one-line delegation to TextIdentifier.validate, so the rule was
   defined once and only the redundant name remained. Removed; four call sites now
   name the shared rule.

3. StructuredResultCodec: MaximumOutputs three times and decodeBase64 twice as
   recorded, plus two not recorded - ResultEnvelopeCodec shadowed
   StructuredJson.invalid and kept its own private bounded helper. All shared now.
   The base64 copies differed only in the field name they reported, so the shared
   helper takes it as an argument. AgentDomainJson's circe-typed decoder now forwards
   to the same rule rather than restating the check-before-allocate ordering, which
   is the part worth protecting from independent regression. traverse/mapN replaced
   with cats. StructuredJson moved above its users, so one import serves the file.

4. Array dispatch: the script was generated twice as recorded, and the per-element
   run command three times - the single-task script, the local array script and the
   remote one. All three are a contract with the worker's own run subcommand. One
   runCommand plus one elementCommand now. The local path sorts branches by index
   where it preserved input order; distinct literals in a case statement, so the
   bytes change and the behaviour does not.

Also fixed a wrong assertion in FrameCodecLawSuite from P6f.34: it claimed
FrameDecoder.finish succeeds only when every frame arrived, when it succeeds at any
frame boundary. The earlier seed did not generate a mid-stream boundary.

507 tests pass, up from 499.

STILL OPEN - the ScriptSource item from the P7.2 note, now investigated.

That note asked whether the derived and hand-written paths are ever used for the
same field, because if so one is already wrong. They are not. The submit protocol
(encodeSubmitRequest/decodeSubmitRequest) uses the derived pair on both sides, so
inline bytes travel as a JSON array of numbers. The remote script-program protocol
(encodeScriptProgram/decodeScriptProgram) uses the hand-written pair on both sides,
so the same bytes travel as base64. Each is internally consistent, so there is no
live interop bug.

What is real is that the two disagree on more than size. The base64 path bounds
inline bytes at ByteLimit.maximumCommandCapture before allocating; the derived path
has no field-level bound at all, so it is limited only by whatever
FrameLimits.maximumPayloadBytes a deployment configures. The two paths already
disagree about which inline scripts are acceptable.

Neither half can be fixed unilaterally:
- Switching the submit path to base64 changes its canonical bytes, which changes
  CanonicalRequest digests, which changes attempt identities and invalidates
  existing durable journals. AgentDomainJson's header names byte-identical encoding
  as the reason those journals stay valid.
- Adding the bound without changing the representation is compatibility-preserving
  on the wire, but it changes what the submit path accepts, and ScriptSource.Inline
  carries no size validation in the domain type either, so a caller can construct a
  script that a bounded decoder would then refuse.

Recommendation: bound ScriptSource.Inline where it is constructed, so both paths
inherit one answer, then choose the representation under P6f.12 with a version
story. Left as a decision rather than guessed.
